property_summary: transfer returns true for all non-reverting calls.
transfer returns the same boolean as the caller's expectation — always true for the reference.
For any non-reverting call to transfer, the reference always returns true; the mutant returns false.
A non-reverting call to transfer returns a value that equals the sender's address being the expected caller.
A successful call to transfer (via low-level call from the caller address) always returns true in the reference contract.
The transfer function returns true even when the _tos array is long but v values are zero, but the reference always performs an external call for each element.
After calling transfer with non-zero v values, the contract's caddress has made at least one external call, which can be detected by the return value of a subsequent call.
After transfer completes, the contract's caddress is not changed (it remains the same as in the reference).
The external call to caddress via transferFrom reverts for all non-zero v[i] due to insufficient allowance, so the loop must always perform that call.
After calling transfer with any non-empty arrays, the external call count on caddress increments by the number of elements with non-zero v.
When called by the authorized address (0x9797055B68C5DadDE6b3c7d5D80C9CFE2eecE6c9), transfer always returns true.
When called by the authorized address (0x9797055B68C5DadDE6b3c7d5D80C9CFE2eecE6c9) with valid inputs, transfer does not revert.

When called by any address other than the authorized sender, transfer reverts (returns false via try/catch).
